name: permissions.py
summary: Custom DRF permission class that grants access only to the dataset's owner.
purpose: Enforces object-level authorization to ensure users can only read or modify datasets they own, preventing unauthorized cross-tenant data access.
responsibilities: Evaluate whether the requesting user owns the target dataset object
Integrate with Django REST Framework's permission framework by subclassing BasePermission
Provide reusable, declarable authorization logic for dataset views
inputs: request (DRF Request object containing the authenticated user)
obj (Dataset model instance to authorize against)
outputs: boolean (True if the user is the dataset owner, False otherwise)
architecture_notes: Implements the Access Control / Authorization layer using the Django REST Framework object-level permission pattern. By inheriting from BasePermission and isolating ownership checks, it keeps authorization concerns decoupled from view business logic and enables declarative composition through permission_classes. It assumes the dataset model exposes an ownership attribute (e.g., owner, user, or created_by) that is compared against request.user.
improvements: Add support for shared or team-based ownership beyond a single user
Allow superusers or staff members to bypass ownership checks for administrative operations
Add explicit logging or monitoring for permission denials to improve security observability
Add configurability for the ownership field name to avoid tight coupling to a specific model attribute
